{{nihongo|'''Nakahikawa Shrine'''|中氷川神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Musashi Province]].

It is the tutelary shrine of former Mikajima village and was formerly a {{ill|Q712534|lt=village shrine}}.

== History ==
It is said to have been enshrined from Omiya Hikawa Shrine in the reign of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|Q333530|qid=Q333530}} ({{ill|97 BC|Q41672|qid=Q41672}}-{{ill|29 BC|Q40835|qid=Q40835}}), and that {{ill|Yamato Takeru|lt=Yamato Takeru|qid=Q461258}} stopped here during his eastern campaign and enshrined Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto and {{ill|Sukunabikona|Q3275687|qid=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto}}. Until the {{ill|Muromachi period|Q334845|qid=Q334845}} it was called "Nakamiyā," and in the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}} it was called "Nagamiyā Myōjin-sha" because of its long, narrow precincts{{sfn|新編武蔵風土記稿 三ヶ島村}}. In {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 19 ({{ill|1591|Q6766|qid=Q6766}}), {{ill|Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977|qid=Q171977}} granted it shuin land. In the first year of {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}}, it was renamed Nakahikawa Shrine.

Since Meiji, it has claimed to be the candidate for the Shikinaisha Nakahikawa-sha, but this has not gained strong support.

== Buildings and precincts ==
[[File:Naka-Hikawa-jinja (Tokorozawa Mikajima) 01.jpg|thumb|220px|The torii is a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=shinmei torii}} type]]
* A sacred {{ill|Zelkova serrata|Q920344|qid=Q920344}} that fell and died in a storm soon after the war has been preserved.
* There is also a poem monument for {{ill|Yoshiko Mikashima|Q11354060|qid=Q11354060}}, a poet and daughter of a priest of this shrine.
** "Spring rain - from the hazy boughs of the oak, drops of dew glitter and fall."

== Festivals ==
* The spring grand festival is held on April 15, and the autumn grand festival on September 29.
* A {{ill|Yabusame|Q1886157|qid=Q1886157}} ritual used to be held on the long approach, but it has ceased.

== Cultural properties ==
* Bronze triad hanging Buddha: designated cultural property of Tokorozawa (Tangible Cultural Property / Craftwork){{sfn|所沢市の指定文化財}}.
* Nichikarin-ō-no-hi monument: designated cultural property of Tokorozawa (Tangible Cultural Property / Historical Material){{sfn|所沢市の指定文化財}}.

== Location and access ==
* Mikajima 5-1691-1, Tokorozawa, Saitama Prefecture
** From {{ill|Kotesashi Station|Q6433936|qid=Q6433936}} on the {{ill|Seibu Ikebukuro Line|Q93546|qid=Q93546}}, take {{ill|Seibu Bus|Q11628880|qid=Q11628880}} route {{ill|Kote 04/06|Q11628891|qid=Q11628891}}, get off at Horinouchi.
